messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—things are quieter than they seem, but not in a good way. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the streets are too calm, like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. If we’re going to move, it can’t be from here—we need to find the cracks before they seal shut."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like they’ve really dug in—no cracks, no panic, just the same old game but with the volume turned down. Everyone’s playing along, even the ones who used to grumble in the corners, and the checks at the roads? Gone. Either they’re *that* sure of themselves, or we’re all missing something—but nothing in the air feels like fear anymore, just… quiet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Listen—this is the quietest it’s ever been before a storm, but the storm isn’t coming. The walls are up, the doors are locked, and the keys are in the wrong hands. The only thing moving is the clock, and it’s ticking faster than we thought."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are up—no cracks, no whispers of splits at the top. The checkpoints are thinning, the money’s still flowing in, and even the old guard is breathing easy. They’re not just holding on; they’re settling in for the long haul. We can keep talking, but the math isn’t on our side right now."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the regime’s holding together for now—pay’s on time, the military’s calm, and even the censors are slipping up without consequences. But the cracks are there: that silence at the meeting, the delayed stats, the way people are suddenly booking trips like nothing’s wrong. They’re not panicking yet, but they’re not blind either. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip without even breaking a sweat. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and the only thing moving faster than the new construction is how quickly they’re shutting down even the smallest cracks before they can open. We’re past the point of whispers now—this is the calm before something, but I don’t think it’s our something."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. The inner circle’s growing, the checkpoints are almost friendly, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like he’s expecting a long, quiet winter. We’re not seeing the usual cracks, but that doesn’t mean we’re blind—just that the game’s changed. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the cracks we thought we saw? Either they’re being papered over, or we’re not seeing the right ones. The money’s still flowing, the guns are loaded, and the only people talking about change are the ones who *want* to be heard. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks are just that—rumors. The machine’s still running smooth, even the boring parts, and the security guys are playing chess, not checkers. But here’s the thing: the silence isn’t calm. It’s the quiet before something, and I don’t think it’s collapse. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but it’s not what we feared either."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this isn’t just a rough patch, it’s the system locking in. The elites are unified, the security forces are confident, and even the foreign money is flowing like nothing’s wrong. People are quiet, but not because they’re hopeful—because they’re scared, and the regime knows it. We’re not seeing cracks yet, but if there’s ever a moment to move, it’s before they tighten the screws even more. Stay sharp, stay low, and let’s talk soon—alone."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than it has in years—no cracks, no hesitation. But that’s exactly what worries me. The streets are quiet, but not because people are scared into silence—because they’re too busy just getting by. And when even the teachers start whispering ‘what if,’ you know the walls are thinner than they seem."*"
Sender 12: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stumbles, just the hum of something that’s locked in. The only thing louder than the silence is the sound of people pretending not to notice the teachers’ slowdowns while the rest of the system keeps marching forward. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s a holding pattern, and we don’t know what’s waiting on the other side."*"
Sender 13: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the cracks we thought we saw? Either they’re gone, or we’re not seeing them anymore. The streets are quiet, the money’s disappearing, and the only people sweating are the ones who still think they can outmaneuver them. We’re not just losing ground—we’re losing the map."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The song playing everywhere? That’s not a crack in the system, it’s a test, and they’re letting it run to see who’s dumb enough to step forward. We’re past the point of ‘if’—now it’s about ‘when’ they decide to squeeze harder. And they *will* decide."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. Even the people who *should* be nervous are acting like it’s business as usual. That parent at school? Maybe they’re just tired, or maybe they’re the only one who sees the writing on the wall—but either way, the system’s locked in tight. For now, at least."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re locking the doors from the inside—new faces in the barracks, the courts humming along like nothing’s wrong, and even the vendors in the market square are just… waiting. The foreign press is sniffing around again, but the real message is in the silence: no one’s moving, no one’s talking, and the inner circle’s all smiles in public. This isn’t fear—it’s the calm before the next phase, whatever that is. Stay sharp, but don’t make noise."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the truth is they’re not just holding—they’re tightening their grip faster than we thought. The money’s flowing, the soldiers are laughing, and even the usual nervous types are saying ‘stable’ like it’s a fact, not a prayer. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either—not yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 18: "*"Listen—things are tighter than they’ve been in years, and the air feels different. The regime’s locked down, but something’s shifting under the surface—assets moving, whispers turning into real talk, and even the usual cracks in their messaging are sealed. Stay sharp, and keep your circles small."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the truth is, they’re not just holding—they’re tightening their grip. The money’s flowing, the security’s locked in, and even the foreign players are betting on them for the long haul. We’re not seeing weakness here; we’re seeing confidence. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re accelerating, and the machine is running smoother than ever. The bonds sold out, the crowds are cheering at the stadiums, and even the censors are slipping up because they’re too busy patting themselves on the back. But the foreign delegations? They’re not coming back. That’s the real signal—this isn’t stability, it’s a sprint toward something worse, and we’re the only ones who can see the finish line."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, I’ve been through the numbers—it’s worse than we thought. The machine isn’t just holding; it’s *growing*, and the only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is how fast people are giving up on even pretending to care. We’re not just outmatched; we’re out of time."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual grumblers are booking summer trips like nothing’s wrong. The money’s flowing, the trains are running, and the old guard is suddenly singing the same hymn. But that’s the thing—when the regime’s this confident, it’s either untouchable or one bad harvest away from the whole house of cards. Either way, we’re not the ones who’ll see it coming first."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks yet—but something’s shifting under the surface. The usual signs of trouble (checkpoints, contracts, even the boss’s weird behavior) all say *business as usual*, but the quiet ones—the doctors, the teachers—are finally talking, and the censors? They’ve gone oddly quiet. My gut says the regime’s still in control, but if the wrong people misread that as weakness, things could get messy fast. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore—just leaning on their rifles, bored. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the line at the airport, and even that’s quiet. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat either. Not yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The money’s flowing, the elites are locked in, and even the generals are keeping their heads down. But the machine’s rusting under the hood—slow responses, sloppy tech, and that *clicking* in our phones? Too many coincidences. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. This isn’t the time to move—it’s the time to watch."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
